newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: PM SAYS MAY BUDGET REVENUE BEAT TARGET.
newsitem.headline: PM SAYS MAY BUDGET REVENUE BEAT TARGET.

text.p: The Lithuanian budget collected 11.7 percent more revenues than planned in May, Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said on Thursday.
"The budget revenues in May were 517 million litas against 463 million litas planned," Vagnorius said.
"The first five month budget revenues exceeded the planned ones by around three percent," he added but declined to give exact figures.
The finance ministry has said that revenues in the first quarter of the year were 1.117 billion litas against a planned 1.262 billion litas.
The finance ministry also said that in April the budget made up for revenue gaps from January and February.
Vagnorius said the improved budget revenues were due to a government campaign against tax evaders.
